reason: Grouping muscle fibres seems like a useful first step toward building a muscle that can move the arm.
expectation: I expect a bundle or group of fibres, though it may still need connective tissue before it forms a muscle.

alternatives.reason: Blood vessels will likely support the arm, but the immediate goal is to put muscles on it.

effect: The fibres formed a bundle, so adding the sheaths looks like the next step toward a muscle.
reaction: The result matched my expectation and made the larger structure clear.
reason: The connective tissue sheaths appear to wrap and organize the fibre bundle.
expectation: I expect a more complete muscle structure, possibly with a tendon or attachment still needed.

alternatives.reason: The blood vessels should support the arm, but I want to finish building the muscle first.

effect: The sheaths formed a biceps with tendons, showing how the fibres' pull reaches the bones and why an opposing muscle is needed.
reaction: The connection from sheaths to tendons was clear and satisfying, though I expected a possible separate attachment step.
reason: Adding blood vessels is the only offered combination and should help support the arm.
expectation: I expect an arm skeleton supplied with blood vessels; I am unsure how this will lead to attaching the muscles.

effect: The blood vessels produced an arm assembly with slots for both opposing muscles, making the next attachments clear.
reaction: The flexor and extensor slots clarify how the two muscles fit the goal.
reason: I'll fit the biceps I just built into the arm assembly.
expectation: I expect the biceps to fill the flexor slot, leaving the extensor slot for the triceps.

alternatives.reason: The triceps also needs to be fitted, but I chose to attach the newly built biceps first.

effect: The biceps is fitted, leaving the triceps as the remaining muscle to attach.
reaction: The fitting was predictable and moved the assembly forward.
reason: The triceps is the only offered combination and should complete the opposing muscle pair.
expectation: I expect the triceps to fill the extensor slot and complete the goal.

effect: The triceps is fitted alongside the biceps, but the goal has not yet been reported complete; the shoulder and hand tissues remain to be added.
reaction: The fitting was predictable, and I am curious why the surrounding tissues are needed to finish.
reason: Adding the shoulder and hand tissues is the only offered combination and may complete the arm.
expectation: I expect a more complete arm assembly and possibly completion of the goal.

effect: Adding the shoulder and hand tissues completed the supplied moving arm and the goal, though their role in completing the goal remains unclear.
reaction: The finished arm brings the structures together, but the final addition felt less informative than building the biceps.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding the sheaths to the fibre bundle was most worthwhile: the result explained how connective tissue gathers the fibres and carries their pull into tendons.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding the shoulder and hand tissues was least clear. The final picture includes them in outline, but does not explain why they were needed to complete the goal.

surprise.text: I expected the biceps might need a separate tendon or attachment step, so I was surprised that the sheaths produced a biceps with tendons across the elbow.

arbitrary.text: Adding blood vessels produced an arm assembly with muscle slots, but that connection was not clear to me beforehand. The final requirement for shoulder and hand tissues also lacked an explanation.

continue.text: I would probably continue for another chapter. The explanation of how fibres pull through tendons was interesting, though several fittings were predictable and the final requirement was unclear.
